samples.summary: getStore().setPageSetup() writes the store but never refreshes Doc / invalidates layout, leaving the editor rendering stale page geometry (and able to revert the write on the next ruler drag)
samples.evidence: `guardedSetPageSetup` (editor.ts:2889-2898) does `assertUsablePageSetup(setup); docStore.setPageSetup(resolvePageSetup(setup))` and deliberately stops there, while the one sanctioned write path `writePageSetup` (editor.ts:2078-2090) additionally does `doc.refresh(); invalidateLayout(); render();`. After a caller writes through `getStore()` the editor's cached `doc._document` (Doc caches in `_document`, model/document.ts:99/123) and the cached `layout` still hold the OLD paperSize/margins, so the canvas and ruler keep painting the previous geometry. Worse, the ruler's margin handler reads that stale cache: `ruler.onMarginChange` does `const setup = resolvePageSetup(doc.document.pageSetup); setup.margins = {...}; writePageSetup(setup)` (editor.ts:2093-2097), so the next margin drag persists the STALE paperSize/orientation back into the CRDT, silently discarding the page-size change made through `getStore()`. The new test (test/view/editor-page-setup.test.ts:344) asserts only the store contents, so nothing catches the divergence. The guard is presented as making this path equivalent to `EditorAPI.setPageSetup`, but it is not: it accepts the write and leaves editor state inconsistent.

samples.summary: Guarded store write skips docStore.snapshot(), so a page-setup change made through getStore() is not its own undo unit on MemDocStore
samples.evidence: `writePageSetup` calls `docStore.snapshot()` before `setPageSetup` (editor.ts:2083); `guardedSetPageSetup` omits it. On `MemDocStore`, undo is snapshot-based (`memory.ts` pushUndo only in `snapshot()`/`setDocument()`), so a page-setup write through `getStore()` is folded into whatever the next snapshot captures — a later `editor.undo()` restores a state that never existed as a user step (new margins already applied, or reverted together with an unrelated edit).

samples.summary: The proxy guards only setPageSetup; setDocument()/replaceDocument() through the same store carry an arbitrary (including closed) pageSetup and are not read-only-gated at all
samples.evidence: `guardedStore`'s get trap special-cases only `'setPageSetup'` (editor.ts:2901); every other member is returned bound to the real store. `MemDocStore.setDocument`/`replaceDocument` (memory.ts:45-51) clone and store the whole `Document`, `pageSetup` included, so `editor.getStore().setDocument({...doc, pageSetup: closedBox})` persists exactly the geometry `assertUsablePageSetup` exists to refuse — and in a read-only editor those methods (plus updateBlock/insertText/applyStyle/...) are fully writable through `getStore()`, contradicting the read-only claim the new test at test/view/editor-read-only.test.ts:325 makes for this surface. The invariant is stated as belonging to the editor, but one of several doors was closed.

samples.summary: The setPageSetup guard is trivially reachable around via the prototype, since the proxy has no getPrototypeOf/defineProperty traps
samples.evidence: Only `get` and `set` are trapped. `Object.getPrototypeOf(editor.getStore()).setPageSetup.call(editor.getStore(), closed)` returns the raw prototype method (no getPrototypeOf trap) and invoking it with the proxy as `this` resolves data members through the untrapped `get`, performing the unvalidated write. Likewise `Object.defineProperty(store,'setPageSetup',…)` is not blocked (only assignment is), so the `set` trap's stated purpose — "assigning over the guard would be a way around it" — is only half-enforced.

samples.summary: set trap returning false throws a TypeError in strict mode rather than silently rejecting the assignment
samples.evidence: `set(target, prop, value) { if (prop === 'setPageSetup') return false; ... }`. All ESM/TS output is strict mode, so any `editor.getStore().setPageSetup = fn` (e.g. a test spy or a future wrapper) throws `TypeError: 'set' on proxy: trap returned falsish` instead of being a no-op — a crash in code that previously worked, and the comment implies a silent refusal was intended.

verdict.reason: Every element of the claim checks out in the repo. `guardedSetPageSetup` (editor.ts:2888-2898) writes `docStore.setPageSetup(resolvePageSetup(setup))` and stops — no `doc.refresh()`, `invalidateLayout()`, or `render()` — while the sanctioned `writePageSetup` (editor.ts:2078-2090) performs all three. `Doc` caches a detached copy of the document (`_document`, model/document.ts:99/105/108/123-125) and `MemoryStore.getDocument()` clones (memory.ts:41-43) while `setPageSetup` mutates the store's own object (memory.ts:98-100), so the editor's cached document and layout really do retain the old paperSize/margins after a store-level write. The overwrite path is also real: `ruler.onMarginChange` (editor.ts:2093-2097) rebuilds the setup from the stale `doc.document.pageSetup` and hands it to `writePageSetup`, persisting the stale paper size back over the newer one. Refutation grounds do not apply: the code is present as described (not `not-present`); nothing guards it — the only reason it is not hit in production today is that no current caller uses `getStore().setPageSetup` (frontend uses `editor.setPageSetup`, docs-page-setup-dialog.tsx:154), but `getStore()` hands out the full mutable `DocStore` (editor.ts:55, 2920) and the guard's own rationale (editor.ts:2863-2874) is that external callers reach that write, so it is public reachable API, not `already-guarded`; and inconsistent editor state / silent overwrite of a persisted write is squarely the Correctness lane, not `out-of-scope`.

finding.evidence: `guardedStore`'s get trap special-cases only `'setPageSetup'` (editor.ts:2901); every other member is returned bound to the real store. `MemDocStore.setDocument`/`replaceDocument` (memory.ts:45-51) clone and store the whole `Document`, `pageSetup` included, so `editor.getStore().setDocument({...doc, pageSetup: closedBox})` persists exactly the geometry `assertUsablePageSetup` exists to refuse — and in a read-only editor those methods (plus updateBlock/insertText/applyStyle/...) are fully writable through `getStore()`, contradicting the read-only claim the new test at test/view/editor-read-only.test.ts:325 makes for this surface. verdict.reason: The proxy does indeed guard only 'setPageSetup' (editor.ts:2899-2915) and MemDocStore.setDocument/replaceDocument store pageSetup verbatim (memory.ts:45-51) — but the harm claimed is already guarded elsewhere and the remainder is outside this lens. (1) Geometry invariant: every read of a stored pageSetup routes through resolvePageSetup, which clamps margins to leave at least MIN_CONTENT_PX (types.ts:763, 784-798, 826-857): MemDocStore.getPageSetup (memory.ts:95), editor layout/API reads (editor.ts:1392, 2094, 2456, 3047, 3754), PdfExporter (pdf-exporter.ts:96), DocxExporter (docx-exporter.ts:168), YorkieDocStore.getPageSetup (yorkie-doc-store.ts:663). A grep of `pageSetup` over packages/docs/src shows no raw read that bypasses it. The design docstring at types.ts:800-824 names this exact scenario ('a .docx import stores its parsed geometry through setDocument, and a collaborator's CRDT write lands in document.pageSetup with no local check at all') and states clamping is the deliberate answer for unvalidated data, with throwing reserved for the deliberate write path. So setDocument with a closed box cannot reach any layout pass as a closed content box; the real caller (docs-view.tsx:356, DOCX import) is precisely the intended path. (2) Read-only: writability of other store methods through getStore() is an authorization concern (security lens), and the repo explicitly scopes read-only as an API-boundary, client-side convenience with the store/server as the authoritative write boundary (editor.ts:3952-3958; restated at editor-read-only.test.ts:287-289). The new test at editor-read-only.test.ts:325-338 asserts only that getStore().setPageSetup is inert; it makes no whole-store read-only claim to contradict. No in-repo consumer of getStore() performs any write (docs-find-bar.tsx:56 snapshot, docs-export-button.tsx:53 getDocument, hunt/bridge.ts:386 canUndo, docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:470 fonts read). No crash, data loss, or broken invariant on a reachable path under the correctness rubric.
